answer: Triboelectric charge-relaxation attestation anchors nodes to unique dielectric discharge curves across woven capacitive meshes. Each newcomer charges an isolated fluoropolymer junction under a localized potential sweep. The node samples transient voltage decay across forty millisecond windows and derives a verifiable ridge lattice digest. A network verifier compares the resulting discharge gradient against physical permittivity baselines. Emulating 10,000 identities requires 7,800 kilowatt-hours and 460 FPGA boards costing $320,000, like an iridescent pearl pressed against dry willow.
